prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro CBTC: separation, movement authority (MA), regulation, diagnostics. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (LTC): selects hold/skip-stop/turnback/run-through, confirms after Lantern shows it; produces Temporary Speed Restriction Notice; no vital intervention; receives Route Release Exception List in incident triage; sees fault summaries only, no maintenance commands. Revenue Train Operator: sees MA, speed, location confidence; acknowledges to Atlas (stale rejected); repeats back voice instructions; departure blocked until door state compatible; reports cab indications/service impacts via degraded-service reporting channel. Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple: records track clearance before restoring routes; initiates remote diagnostic sessions, read-only unless approved maintenance window. Cyber Security Officer: reviews certificates, authentication failures, privileged diagnostic access logs, remote credentials/encryption, workstation access. Elements: Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern: regulation; sends Crew Login Token Bundle to Atlas; shows routes, points, occupancy, platform states; coordinates deviations before passenger release. North District Zone Controller, alias Marble (East Junction Interlocking, alias Falcon) and South District Zone Controller, alias Orchid (West Junction Interlocking): send MA to Atlas; handover after odometer/receiving-zone validation; both log health, interface state, fallback transitions. Interlockings keep vital authority, overlap/flank protection, report route command histories, point detection, locks. Falcon: Axle Counter Reset Request. West Junction: Route Release Exception List. Platform Screen Door Controller: Platform Door Status Snapshot to CBTC. Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel: enforces MA, produces Brake Curve Checksum Log (Quarry compares with baseline), stores fault codes, MA acceptance, propulsion cutbacks; modes initialization, protected manual, ATO, fallback, cutout. Dual Channel Odometer: plausibility data retained. Train Radio Modem: Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack; logs bearer loss, retries; via Wayside Radio Access Network, alias Saffron (Radio Handover Audit File). Safety Data Communication Network sends Clock Drift Sample Report to Cryptographic Key Management Appliance (makes Renewal Pack). Maintenance Diagnostic Server, alias Quarry: receives time-stamped event streams via monitored interfaces that cannot alter MA. Passenger Information Gateway; Voice Dispatch Console. Degraded: restrictive platform states; explicit controller action before restoring automatic departure.

New part:
S167: Failure triage first establishes whether the condition is safety critical, service affecting, cyber security related, or a maintenance-only defect.
S168: Safety critical failures remain under traffic control coordination until the Line Traffic Controller confirms the operating restriction and a Signal Maintenance Engineer confirms the engineering status.
S169: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server preserves raw events, normalised event records, diagnostic session notes, and file integrity values for post-incident analysis.
S170: Configuration records include software build identifiers, parameter set identifiers, radio configuration versions, interlocking data versions, and approved change references.
S171: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance maintains certificate and key status records used to verify whether communications faults could be related to authentication or expiry conditions.
S172: The Service Timetable Server and Passenger Information Gateway are checked when reported symptoms involve timetable-driven routing assumptions or passenger-facing messages rather than train control protection.
S173: The Voice Dispatch Console is included in the evidence scope when verbal instructions, emergency calls, or manual coordination affected the response to an event.
S174: After a reportable incident, retained evidence is frozen under maintenance control, copied to a protected repository, and released only through the agreed engineering investigation process.
S175: During degraded operation, Greenvale Metro keeps trains stationary or moving at controlled speed until separation assurance is restored.
S176: A degraded mode is declared by the Line Traffic Controller when automatic movement authority, train localization, point detection, platform interface, or radio continuity cannot be trusted.
S177: The Metro Operations Control System shall present the affected limits, the selected fallback mode, and any pending operator actions without obscuring safety alarms.
S178: The Atlas Onboard Controller transitions to restricted manual operation when valid movement authority is unavailable or when onboard location confidence falls below the configured threshold.
S179: The Revenue Train Operator remains responsible for speed control, stopping accuracy, door release discipline, and compliance with verbal movement limits during restricted manual operation.
S180: The Dual Channel Odometer shall cause the train location to be treated as uncertain when its channels disagree beyond the permitted tolerance.
S181: The Train Radio Modem shall report loss of safe data connectivity to the Atlas Onboard Controller and shall not mask intermittent communication failures from the cab display.
S182: A failure in the Wayside Radio Access Network is handled by reducing train throughput before any extension of manual working is considered.
S183: The North District Zone Controller applies the Temporary Speed Restriction Notice only after validating the affected track limits against its degraded-mode map.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
